The encoding fixes are correct. `quote(..., safe="")` turns spaces into `%20`, leaves `-._~` as they are and encodes UTF-8 bytes as uppercase hex, and booleans are now written as `true`/`false`. Both match the docstring.

However, the PR sorts keys alphabetically (`sorted(params.keys())`), and that breaks the documented rule: "Parameters are written in the iteration order of `params`." The only reason for the sort is to satisfy `test_search_request`, whose expected value (`limit=20&page=2&q=coffee` from `{"q", "page", "limit"}` input) contradicts the docstring. The teammate named the docstring as the source of truth. Sorting also introduces a `TypeError` when keys are of mixed types, and it silently reorders parameters for every caller, which can matter to some partner APIs. There's also no PR description, so the conflict was never flagged.

Please go back to `params.items()` order and keep the `quote` and boolean fixes. Then tell the teammate that `test_search_request` conflicts with the documented contract instead of making the code match that one test.
